_schema.about: All game data for Borealis. Formulas live in spec/game-systems.md section 13 and are implemented in spec/balance/engine.py (reference engine). Numbers here are game-scale, not real-world values. Money is in $B (billions of Borealis dollars). Goods are in units.

conventions.ids: lower case, no spaces. Province ids are locked by the brief.
conventions.levels: Tax and spending use levels 1 to 5. Level 3 is Standard. Arrays indexed by level use index 0 for level 1.
conventions.groups: Citizen group ids: workers, families, businesses, seniors.
conventions.resources: Resource ids: food, energy, materials, money. Only food, energy and materials are goods. Money is the treasury.
conventions.studentText: Any field named text, label, hint or headline is student-facing. Grade 8 reading level, second person, no em dashes.

_schema.constants: Formula constants. See game-systems.md section 13 for where each one is used.
_schema.citizenGroups: The four groups that make up approval. taxWeight scales how much a tax change moves the group.
_schema.spendingCategories: Four provincial spending lines. groupWeight scales the level effect for each group.
_schema.economicSystems: Five steps from market (1) to command (5). prodMult: goods production multiplier. baseUnemployment: percent. growth: yearly service growth in percent points. shockMult: scales national event production hits. plannerShift: goods units the group may move by hand each year. marketShift: units the market moves on its own toward the highest price. scarcityShare: who feels a shortage most. approvalPerYear: yearly approval change for each group from the system alone.
_schema.provinces: Starting state. production and needs are goods units per year. services is yearly money output of the service economy in $B. spendingBaseline is the cost of each line at Standard (level 3) when CPI is 100. costFactor raises all spending costs (Northreach is remote). debt is net debt in $B (negative means savings). groupShare sums to 1.
_schema.investmentProjects: Optional one-off projects from Year 4. Cost is a percent of this year's revenue (the app shows it in $B). Usually paid by borrowing. Effects are permanent.

type.money: amount ($B) or pctRevenue (percent of this year's revenue). Negative is a cost. Paid at year end. years repeats it.
type.approval: group (workers, families, businesses, seniors or all) and amount (points).
type.production: resource and pct. Multiplies goods production for the year(s).
type.baseProduction: resource and amount (units). Permanent change from next year.
type.need: resource and amount (units) or pct. Changes yearly needs.
type.growth: amount (percent points) added to this year's growth.
type.inflation: amount (percent points) added to this year's inflation.
type.price: resource and mult. National price multiplier for this year. Events only.
type.cost: category (health, education, infrastructure, social or all) and pct. Changes spending cost.
type.skill: amount. Adds to the province skill level (education stock).
type.infrastructure: amount. Adds to the province infrastructure stock.
type.interestRate: amount (percent points) added to the debt interest rate.
type.tradeFee: pct added to the interprovincial trade fee. Optional routes list limits it to some routes.

effects.target: self (default), all, others, a province id, or a list of province ids.
effects.start: now (default) or next. Card choices are made after Income, so production and services effects from choices always start next year.
effects.years: How many years the effect lasts (default 1).
effects.ifSpending: { category, atLeast, scale }. If the province set that line at or above the level this year, multiply the effect by scale.

_schema.cards: localIssues: province cards (province set) and general cards (province null). nationalEvents: auto effects hit listed provinces when revealed; every province then picks one choice. bridgeCrisis: the period 9 card.
_schema.deck: Default order of cards by year. The teacher can swap any card before revealing it.
_schema.parties: Four preset federal parties. spectrum uses the same 1 to 5 scale as economicSystems. planks feed the election model (appeal) and the federal budget (budgetLevers).
_schema.regionalPromises: Pool of one promise per province. Each party may adopt one.
_schema.ridingTypes: Citizen group mix by riding type. Sums to 1.
_schema.ridings: 34 ridings. Seats per province follow population.
_schema.election: Constants for the election model. See game-systems.md section 9.
_schema.federalBudget: Lever options for the federal budget bill and their effects on provinces in Year 7.
_schema.bills: Bills for Phase 2. The budget bill is required.
_schema.scoring: Reasoning points, awards and the class goal.
_schema.periods: Default 16-period flow with step timings in minutes.

resources.name: Energy
resources.text: Power for homes and factories. Without enough energy, factories slow down and people lose jobs.

resources.name: Food
resources.text: Everyone needs to eat. When food is short, prices rise and people get angry fast.

resources.name: Materials
resources.text: Wood, metal and minerals. You need them to build roads, homes and schools.

resources.name: Money
resources.text: Your government's treasury. It comes from taxes and from selling goods.

citizenGroups.name: Workers
citizenGroups.text: People with jobs in factories, mines, farms, shops and offices. They want good jobs and fair pay.

citizenGroups.name: Families
citizenGroups.text: Parents and kids. They want good schools, health care and prices they can afford.

citizenGroups.name: Businesses
citizenGroups.text: Business owners, from corner stores to big companies. They want low taxes, roads that work and room to grow.

citizenGroups.name: Seniors
citizenGroups.text: Retired people. They want health care, steady prices and a government that does not take big risks.

spendingCategories.name: Education
spendingCategories.otherEffects: Skill changes by (level - 3) each year. Skill adds to growth and lowers unemployment. Pays off slowly.

spendingCategories.name: Infrastructure
spendingCategories.otherEffects: Infrastructure stock changes by (level - 3) each year and raises goods production. Each level above Standard raises the Materials need by 15% (at least 1 unit). Adds growth and jobs this year.

spendingCategories.name: Social programs
spendingCategories.text: Help for people without work, seniors' pensions, child benefits.

economicSystems.name: Market
economicSystems.text: People and businesses decide. Prices tell farms and factories what to make. Government stays small.

threeQuestions.what: Prices decide. The market moves production toward goods that sell for more.
threeQuestions.how: Private businesses compete to make things cheaply.
threeQuestions.forWhom: People who can pay. Shortages hurt workers, families and seniors more.

economicSystems.name: Market-leaning mixed
economicSystems.text: Mostly private business with some government rules and services.

threeQuestions.what: Mostly prices, with a little government planning.
threeQuestions.how: Mostly private businesses, some public services.
threeQuestions.forWhom: Mostly people who can pay, with a basic safety net.

economicSystems.name: Mixed
economicSystems.text: Private businesses run most things. Government runs health care and schools and sets rules.

threeQuestions.what: Prices and government plans share the job.
threeQuestions.how: Private businesses and public services side by side.
threeQuestions.forWhom: Everyone gets basic services. Extras go to those who can pay.

economicSystems.name: Command-leaning mixed
economicSystems.text: Government owns key industries and plans a lot. Some private business is allowed.

threeQuestions.how: Many public companies, some private ones.
threeQuestions.forWhom: Shared more equally. Fewer choices for buyers.

economicSystems.name: Command
economicSystems.text: Government decides what to make, how to make it and who gets it. It owns the farms and factories.

threeQuestions.forWhom: Shared equally by plan. Little personal choice.

traditionalEconomy.where: Local issue card saltmarch-fishing-custom, choice keep-custom.
traditionalEconomy.why: Traditional economies decide by custom and habit, not prices or plans. A province government cannot switch a whole modern economy to tradition, so it does not fit as a setting. A fishing village that shares grounds by custom is a real, neutral historical example in Atlantic regions and lets students compare all three ways of deciding on one card.

provinces.name: Westhaven
provinces.blurb: Mountains, rainforest and the busiest port in Borealis. You have timber and hydro power, but little farmland.

provinces.name: Ridgeland
provinces.blurb: Oil, gas and cattle country. When energy prices are high you boom. When they fall, you feel it first.

provinces.name: Goldplain
provinces.blurb: Wheat, canola and potash. You feed the country, but your small towns have little money and you buy most of your energy.

provinces.name: Lakemoor
provinces.blurb: Factories, banks and the biggest cities. You have the most people and the most money, but you must buy food and energy.

provinces.name: Valcourt
provinces.blurb: Big rivers, hydro dams and aluminum plants. You have your own language and culture. Hard years can leave you short of food.

provinces.name: Saltmarch
provinces.blurb: Fishing towns, shipyards and some offshore oil. Many of your people are older, so health care and pensions cost a lot.

provinces.name: Northreach
provinces.blurb: Huge land, rich mines and very few people. Winters are long and everything costs more to ship in.

investmentProjects.name: New power plant
investmentProjects.text: Borrow to build a power plant. You make more energy every year after.

investmentProjects.name: Modern farms
investmentProjects.text: Help farmers buy better equipment. You grow more food every year after.

investmentProjects.name: Tech college
investmentProjects.text: Build a college for new jobs. It takes time, but your workers get more skilled.

investmentProjects.name: Highway and rail upgrade
investmentProjects.text: Faster roads and trains. Your farms, mines and factories all produce more.

localIssues.title: A Bigger Port?
localIssues.text: Shipping companies want a bigger port in Westhaven. More ships mean more trade and more jobs. People who live near the harbour worry about noise and traffic.

choices.label: Build it with public money
choices.hint: Costs a lot now. Workers and businesses like it.

choices.label: Let a private company build and run it
choices.hint: Free for you. The company sets the fees.

choices.label: Say no for now
choices.hint: Neighbours are happy. Businesses are not.

localIssues.debrief: Who decided how the port is built in each choice: the government or a company?

localIssues.title: The Old Forest
localIssues.text: A timber company wants to cut down an old forest. It would bring jobs and lots of wood. Many people want the forest protected for good.

choices.label: Allow logging
choices.hint: More materials and jobs. Families and seniors are upset.

choices.label: Protect the forest
choices.hint: Families cheer. Forestry workers lose out.

choices.label: Allow some logging with replanting rules
choices.hint: A middle path. Rules cost money to check.

localIssues.debrief: What did your province give up in each choice? That is the trade-off.

localIssues.title: Save It or Spend It?
localIssues.text: Energy companies paid you extra royalties this year, about half a year of tax money more than you planned. Do you save it for hard times, spend it now, or give it back as a tax cut?

choices.label: Save it in a rainy-day fund
choices.hint: Lowers your debt. Nobody sees it right away.

choices.label: Spend it on hospitals and schools
choices.hint: Families and seniors like it now.

choices.label: Give it back as a one-year tax cut
choices.hint: Businesses and workers cheer. The money is gone.

localIssues.debrief: If energy prices fall next year, which choice will you be glad you made?

localIssues.title: A Pipeline to the Coast
localIssues.text: A company wants to build a pipeline from Ridgeland to the Westhaven port. You could sell more energy. Towns along the route worry about spills. Westhaven has to agree to the route.

choices.label: Support the pipeline
choices.hint: More energy sales. Some Westhaven families object.

choices.label: Support it with strict safety rules
choices.hint: Smaller gain. Costs a little. Fewer people upset.

choices.label: Say no
choices.hint: No risk of spills. Energy workers are angry.

localIssues.debrief: Your choice changed another province's approval. Should one province get a say in another's project?

localIssues.title: Small Towns Fading
localIssues.text: Young people are moving from small towns to the cities. Schools, clinics and stores are closing. The people who stay feel left behind.

choices.label: Pay for rural internet and clinics
choices.hint: Costs money. Families and seniors feel cared for.

choices.label: Let towns change on their own
choices.hint: No cost. Some towns will keep shrinking.

choices.label: Pay new businesses to open in small towns
choices.hint: Some cost. Creates jobs.

localIssues.debrief: Who should decide whether a small town survives: the market or the government?

localIssues.title: The Potash Mine Offer
localIssues.text: A large company wants to open a huge potash mine. It would bring jobs and money. It would also use a lot of energy and water.

choices.label: Yes, and give the company low taxes to come
choices.hint: Jobs and materials. The mine uses more energy.

choices.label: Yes, but the province owns part of the mine
choices.hint: Costs money now. Pays you back for years.

choices.label: No mine
choices.hint: Water stays safe. No new jobs.

localIssues.debrief: Choice 1 is closer to a market economy. Choice 2 is closer to command. What is the difference?

localIssues.title: Robots in the Factories
localIssues.text: Car factories want to replace workers with robots. The factories would make more for less. About 2,000 people could lose their jobs.

choices.label: Let the factories decide
choices.hint: More money for the economy. Workers lose jobs.

choices.label: Allow robots and pay to retrain workers
choices.hint: Costs money. Most workers find new jobs.

choices.label: Ban the robots
choices.hint: Jobs stay. Factories fall behind.

localIssues.debrief: Look at GDP and unemployment next year. Did they move in the same direction?

localIssues.title: Traffic Jam City
localIssues.text: Traffic in Lakemoor's biggest city is the worst in Borealis. Trucks sit still. Commuters are angry. Something has to change.

choices.label: Build a new subway line
choices.hint: Expensive. Pays off for years.

choices.label: Charge drivers a fee to enter downtown
choices.hint: Brings in money. Drivers hate it.

choices.label: Do nothing for now
choices.hint: No cost. Everyone stays stuck.

localIssues.debrief: Is borrowing for a subway a good reason to run a deficit? Why?

localIssues.title: Sell the Hydro Power?
localIssues.text: Valcourt's dams make more electricity than you need. A country across the border wants to buy some of it on a long contract.

choices.label: Sign the export deal
choices.hint: Steady money for years. Less energy at home.

choices.label: Keep the power to attract new factories
choices.hint: More jobs and materials at home.

choices.label: Lower power bills for families
choices.hint: Families and seniors save money. The treasury pays.

localIssues.debrief: Each choice answers 'for whom?' differently. Explain one.

localIssues.title: Keep Our Culture Strong
localIssues.text: Valcourt's language and culture are part of what makes it special. Local artists, schools and TV shows ask for more support. Some say the money should go to hospitals first.

choices.label: Fund language and culture programs
choices.hint: Costs money. Families and seniors are proud.

choices.label: Let culture groups raise their own money
choices.hint: No cost. Some programs close.

choices.label: Share the cost with local businesses
choices.hint: Small cost. A bit for everyone.

localIssues.debrief: Is protecting culture a need or a want? Can it be both?

localIssues.title: The Fishing Grounds
localIssues.text: For generations, Saltmarch fishing families have shared the fishing grounds by custom. Each family fishes its own spot, the way their parents did. Now there are fewer fish each year. How should you decide who fishes?

choices.label: Keep the old customs
choices.hint: Tradition decides. Seniors are glad. Fish keep falling.

choices.label: Sell fishing licences to the highest bidder
choices.hint: The market decides. Big boats win. Money now.

choices.label: The government sets a catch limit for every boat
choices.hint: The government decides. Less fish now, more later.

localIssues.debrief: Name the economic system behind each choice: traditional, market or command.

localIssues.title: The Shipyard Contract
localIssues.text: Your shipyard could build ferries for all of Borealis. First it needs an expensive upgrade. Hundreds of jobs depend on it.

choices.label: Borrow to upgrade the shipyard
choices.hint: Big cost now. Jobs and income later.

choices.label: Sell part of the shipyard to a private company
choices.hint: No cost. The company keeps most of the profit.

choices.label: Close the shipyard and retrain workers
choices.hint: Saves money later. Jobs are lost now.

localIssues.debrief: Was borrowing worth it? Check your debt and GDP in two years.

localIssues.title: The Cost of Living
localIssues.text: Food in Northreach costs three times more than in the south. It comes in by plane or on long winter roads. Families are struggling.

choices.label: Pay part of the shipping cost for food
choices.hint: Costs every year it lasts. Families feel the help now.

choices.label: Build community greenhouses
choices.hint: Costs more now. Grows food for years.

choices.label: Hope prices fall on their own
choices.hint: No cost. Families stay angry.

localIssues.debrief: Which choice helps now and which helps later? Which would you pick in a deficit year?

localIssues.title: New Mine, New Town
localIssues.text: A company wants to open a rare metals mine far from any town. It needs a new road and a power line. It would bring many jobs.

choices.label: The province builds the road and power line
choices.hint: Big cost. You own the road. Lots of jobs.

choices.label: Let the company build and own the road
choices.hint: No cost. The company charges to use the road.

choices.label: Wait and study the effect on land and wildlife
choices.hint: No change for now. Workers wanted those jobs.

localIssues.debrief: Who owns the road in each choice? Why does that matter?

localIssues.title: Long Hospital Waits
localIssues.text: People wait months for surgery. Doctors say they need more nurses. A company offers to open private clinics where people can pay to skip the line.

choices.label: Hire more nurses
choices.hint: Costs money. Seniors and families are relieved.

choices.label: Allow private pay clinics
choices.hint: No cost. People who can pay get care faster.

choices.label: Keep things as they are
choices.hint: No cost. Waits get longer.

localIssues.debrief: Private clinics give more choice to some people. Who loses?

localIssues.title: Teachers Want a Raise
localIssues.text: Teachers say classes are too big and pay is too low. They might go on strike next month.

choices.label: Give teachers a raise
choices.hint: Costs money. Schools improve.

choices.label: Hold firm: no raise
choices.hint: Saves money. A strike closes schools for a week.

choices.label: Meet halfway
choices.hint: Some cost. Nobody is thrilled.

localIssues.debrief: Where does the money for a raise come from: taxes, cuts, or borrowing?

localIssues.title: No Place to Live
localIssues.text: Rents are rising fast. More people are living in cars and shelters. Charities say they cannot keep up.

choices.label: Build affordable housing
choices.hint: Big cost. Uses materials. Helps many people.

choices.label: Fund more shelter beds
choices.hint: Small cost. Helps in an emergency only.

choices.label: Leave it to charities and builders
choices.hint: No cost. The problem grows.

localIssues.debrief: Is housing a job for the market, the government, or both?

localIssues.title: A Tech Company Wants a Deal
localIssues.text: A big tech company will move its offices here if you give it a tax break. It would bring good jobs. Local businesses ask why they do not get the same deal.

choices.label: Give the tax break
choices.hint: Less money now. Faster growth later.

choices.label: Say no: same rules for everyone
choices.hint: No cost. The jobs go somewhere else.

localIssues.debrief: Is it fair to give one company a special deal? What does the province get back?

localIssues.title: The Old Town Bridge
localIssues.text: Engineers say the bridge into a small town is unsafe. It is the only road to the school and the grocery store.

choices.label: Repair it now
choices.hint: Costs money and materials. Problem solved.

choices.label: Repair it and charge a toll
choices.hint: Pays for itself. Drivers pay.

choices.label: Close it for now
choices.hint: No cost. A long detour for everyone.

localIssues.debrief: A toll means users pay. Taxes mean everyone pays. Which is fairer?

localIssues.title: Raise the Minimum Wage?
localIssues.text: Workers say they cannot pay rent on the minimum wage. Small businesses say a big raise means fewer jobs.

choices.label: Raise it a lot
choices.hint: Workers cheer. Some small shops cut jobs.

choices.label: Raise it a little
choices.hint: A small win for workers.

choices.label: Leave it alone
choices.hint: Businesses are relieved. Workers are not.

localIssues.debrief: A government rule here limits a business's choice. When is that worth it?

localIssues.title: An Old Power Plant
localIssues.text: Your oldest power plant is wearing out. It also makes the air dirty. Fixing it, replacing it or closing it all have a cost.

choices.label: Build a new, cleaner plant
choices.hint: Big cost. More energy for years.

choices.label: Patch it up
choices.hint: Small cost. The problem comes back.

choices.label: Close it
choices.hint: Cleaner air. Less energy. Some jobs lost.

localIssues.debrief: Which choice is worth borrowing for? Why?

localIssues.title: Grocery Prices Are Up
localIssues.text: Families are shocked at the grocery bill. Some want the government to set a maximum price on basic food.

choices.label: Set a maximum price on basic food
choices.hint: Prices stop rising. Some farms grow less.

choices.label: Send families a grocery benefit
choices.hint: Costs money. Families get help now.

choices.label: Let prices find their own level
choices.hint: No cost. Families are upset.

localIssues.debrief: A price cap is a command economy tool. What happened to the amount of food produced?

localIssues.title: A New Sports Arena
localIssues.text: The local hockey team wants a new arena. The owners want the province to pay for half. Fans love the idea.

choices.label: Pay for half
choices.hint: Costs a lot. Fans and businesses are happy.

choices.label: The owners pay for it all
choices.hint: No cost. The team may move away.

localIssues.debrief: Should public money pay for things a private business will profit from?

localIssues.title: Not Enough Care Homes
localIssues.text: More people are living longer. There are not enough care homes or home-care nurses. Families are worried.

choices.label: Build new care homes
choices.hint: Big cost. Seniors are grateful.

choices.label: Pay for more home-care visits
choices.hint: Smaller cost. Helps many people stay home.

choices.label: Families must sort it out
choices.hint: No cost. Seniors and families are upset.

localIssues.debrief: Who should look after people who cannot look after themselves?

nationalEvents.title: Prairie Drought
nationalEvents.headline: No rain all summer. Crops dry up across the west.
nationalEvents.text: Farms in Goldplain, Ridgeland and Westhaven grow much less food this year. Food prices rise across Borealis.

choices.label: Give your farmers emergency aid
choices.hint: Costs money. Farms recover faster next year.

choices.label: Ask everyone to waste less food
choices.hint: No cost. You need less food this year. People grumble.

choices.label: Let the market handle it
choices.hint: No cost. Prices stay high.

nationalEvents.debrief: The drought hit three provinces. Why did food prices rise everywhere?

nationalEvents.title: Energy Prices Crash
nationalEvents.headline: World oil and gas prices fall by half.
nationalEvents.text: Energy sells for much less this year. Provinces that sell energy earn less. Provinces that buy energy save money.

choices.label: Keep producing and sell cheap
choices.hint: No change. Earn less this year.

choices.label: Cut energy production and wait
choices.hint: Fewer jobs now. More energy next year.

choices.label: Use cheap energy to grow factories
choices.hint: Small cost. Faster growth.

nationalEvents.debrief: The same event helped some provinces and hurt others. Which ones? Why?

nationalEvents.title: Flu Season
nationalEvents.headline: A bad flu spreads across Borealis.
nationalEvents.text: Hospitals fill up and many people miss work. Provinces that spend more on healthcare cope better.

choices.label: Free flu shots for everyone
choices.hint: Costs money. Seniors and families feel safer.

choices.label: Close schools for two weeks
choices.hint: No cost. Parents miss work. Students fall behind.

choices.label: Let people decide for themselves
choices.hint: No cost. More people get sick.

nationalEvents.debrief: Did healthcare spending you chose earlier pay off this year?

nationalEvents.title: Wildfire Season
nationalEvents.headline: Huge fires burn forests in the west and north.
nationalEvents.text: Westhaven, Northreach and Ridgeland lose forests and must pay to fight fires. Firefighters from other provinces could help.

choices.label: Send firefighters to help other provinces
choices.hint: Costs a little. Your people feel proud.

choices.label: Protect your own towns first
choices.hint: No cost.

choices.label: Buy new water bomber planes
choices.hint: Big cost now. Safer for years.

nationalEvents.debrief: Would you borrow money to fight a disaster? This is a crisis deficit.

nationalEvents.title: Car Plants Close
nationalEvents.headline: A global car company shuts plants in Lakemoor and Valcourt.
nationalEvents.text: Thousands of jobs are gone. Shops near the plants lose customers too.

choices.label: Pay for job retraining
choices.hint: Costs money. Workers find new jobs.

choices.label: Run a 'Buy Borealis' campaign
choices.hint: Small cost. Helps a little everywhere.

choices.label: Let the market sort it out
choices.hint: No cost. Workers are angry.

nationalEvents.debrief: One company's choice in another country changed jobs here. What does that tell you?

nationalEvents.title: New Technology Arrives
nationalEvents.headline: New machines and software change how work gets done.
nationalEvents.text: Provinces with skilled workers grow faster. Some old jobs disappear.

choices.label: Invest in tech training
choices.hint: Costs money. Skills rise.

choices.label: Cut taxes for tech companies
choices.hint: Less money now. Faster growth.

choices.label: Protect old jobs with new rules
choices.hint: No cost. Slower growth.

nationalEvents.debrief: Did your education spending pay off this year?

nationalEvents.title: World Recession
nationalEvents.headline: Economies around the world slow down.
nationalEvents.text: Other countries buy less from Borealis. Businesses earn less, so your tax revenue falls. More people need help.

choices.label: Spend on building projects to create jobs
choices.hint: Costs money. Jobs now. Bigger deficit.

choices.label: Tighten the belt: cut office costs
choices.hint: Saves money. Some public jobs lost.

choices.label: Wait it out
choices.hint: No change.

nationalEvents.debrief: Why did your revenue fall even though you kept the same tax rate?

nationalEvents.title: Newcomers Arrive
nationalEvents.headline: War overseas forces families to flee. Many come to Borealis.
nationalEvents.text: Thousands of newcomers arrive. They need homes, schools and health care now. Many are skilled workers ready to fill jobs.

choices.label: Fund language classes and job help
choices.hint: Costs money. Newcomers start work sooner.

choices.label: Provide only the basics
choices.hint: Small cost. Newcomers take longer to settle.

choices.label: Ask charities and volunteers to lead
choices.hint: No cost. Volunteers step up, but it is uneven.

nationalEvents.debrief: Newcomers cost money now and add workers later. How is that like other long-term investments?

nationalEvents.title: Interest Rates Rise
nationalEvents.headline: Lenders around the world raise interest rates.
nationalEvents.text: Borrowing costs more. Provinces with big debts must pay more interest. That money cannot go to schools or hospitals.

choices.label: Make a payment on your debt
choices.hint: Costs money now. Less interest later.

choices.label: Keep spending as planned
choices.hint: No change. Interest eats more of your budget.

choices.label: Sell a government building
choices.hint: Money now. People ask what is next.

nationalEvents.debrief: Why does the same rate rise hurt a province with high debt more?

nationalEvents.title: World Food Prices Jump
nationalEvents.headline: Bad harvests overseas push food prices up everywhere.
nationalEvents.text: Food costs more this year. Provinces that grow extra food earn more. Provinces that buy food pay more.

choices.label: Help families with food costs
choices.hint: Costs money. Families feel it less.

choices.label: Push farmers to sell more
choices.hint: No cost. More food to sell next year.

choices.label: Do nothing
choices.hint: No cost.

nationalEvents.debrief: Was this event good or bad news for your province? Why?

nationalEvents.title: Conflict Overseas
nationalEvents.headline: A war far away blocks shipping lanes.
nationalEvents.text: Ships carrying energy and materials around the world are delayed. Energy and materials cost more this year.

choices.label: Send humanitarian aid
choices.hint: Small cost. Your people feel proud.

choices.label: Build up your own energy supply
choices.hint: Costs money. More energy next year.

choices.label: Stay focused at home
choices.hint: No cost.

nationalEvents.debrief: How can events on the other side of the world change life in Borealis?

bridgeCrisis.title: The Great Narrows Bridge Falls
bridgeCrisis.headline: The only bridge that joins east and west Borealis is closed.
bridgeCrisis.text: The Great Narrows Bridge carries the national highway, the railway and the main power line between Goldplain and Lakemoor. Engineers have closed it. It is not safe. Trade between east and west now takes long detours. A new bridge costs $60B. No single province can pay for it.
bridgeCrisis.location: Between Goldplain and Lakemoor. Map designer: place it on the narrowest crossing of the big lakes.

pledgeRounds.text: Each province decides how much to give. Nobody sees the others' pledges until the reveal.
Talk it out. Change your pledge. Pledges are shown live on the board.

outcomes.short: Not enough money. Pledges are returned. The bridge stays closed.
outcomes.temporary: Enough for a temporary bridge. It reopens for 2 years, then needs $20B a year to keep safe. Nobody is in charge of paying that.
outcomes.note: Either way, the class sees that provinces acting alone cannot fund or run a national project. This leads into the four ways to decide and a federal Parliament.

debrief: Who paid the most? Who paid the least but still uses the bridge?
What would make every province pay its fair share?
Who should decide: one strong leader, a few rich provinces, everyone in a big vote, or elected representatives?

deck.generalDraw: Draw without replacement from the general cards, shuffled with the class seed. A province never sees the same general card twice.
deck.underdog: At the start of each year from Year 2, the province with the lowest approval draws two local cards and picks one.

parties.identity: Keep taxes low, keep government small, and build on what already works.
parties.ideology: Conservative: values individual responsibility, limited government, gradual change and respect for tradition and institutions.

planks.title: Lower taxes for everyone
planks.text: You keep more of what you earn. Families and businesses decide how to spend it.

planks.title: Balance the budget
planks.text: No new debt. We will not leave a bill for your kids.

planks.title: Provinces know best
planks.text: Provinces run health and schools their own way. Federal money comes with no strings attached.

planks.title: Build with business
planks.text: Private partners help build the new bridge and pay part of the cost with tolls. A growth credit helps businesses hire.

parties.identity: Fair chances for everyone, with a government that steps in to help and keeps the books in check.
parties.ideology: Centre-left liberal: values reform, equal opportunity, an active government and a mixed economy.

planks.title: Health care you can count on
planks.text: A bigger health transfer to every province so waits get shorter.

planks.title: Skills for good jobs
planks.text: A national fund for training and college so people can get the jobs of the future.

planks.title: Fair, steady taxes
planks.text: A middle tax rate. A small deficit is fine for investments, then we balance.

planks.title: Rebuild the bridge now
planks.text: Borrow to rebuild the Great Narrows Bridge in two years. Trade moves again fast.

parties.identity: Working people first. Share the wealth so nobody gets left behind.
parties.ideology: Social democratic: values equality, strong public services and a larger role for government in the economy.

planks.title: Support for seniors and families
planks.text: A bigger pension and a child benefit, paid every month.

planks.title: Food for every student
planks.text: A national school food program. No child learns on an empty stomach.

planks.title: Big companies pay their share
planks.text: Higher taxes on the largest companies and highest earners pay for services.

planks.title: Share fairly across Borealis
planks.text: Strong equalization so every province can offer good services.

parties.identity: Protect the land, water and air, and build an economy that lasts for our grandchildren.
parties.ideology: Green: values sustainability, local communities, long-term thinking and grassroots decision making.

planks.title: A clean power grid
planks.text: Connect the country's hydro, wind and solar power with one national grid.

planks.title: Protect land, water and fish
planks.text: Stronger rules for forests, lakes and fisheries so they last.

planks.title: Invest now for the future
planks.text: Borrow for projects that pay back over many years, like clean energy and training.

planks.title: Strong local communities
planks.text: Support for local farms, small businesses and transit in towns and cities.

issueRules.when: CPI rose 12 or more points since Year 1
healthcare at Standard or below for 3 or more years
food was short in 2 or more years
energy was short in 2 or more years
GDP grew less than 8% over Phase 1
province is Valcourt, Northreach or Saltmarch

campaignActions.name: Flyers
campaignActions.effect: +1 appeal in two ridings in the same province

campaignActions.name: Rally
campaignActions.effect: +1 appeal in every riding of one province

campaignActions.name: Get out the vote
campaignActions.effect: +3% turnout in your home riding. No party gets appeal. Anyone can do it.

election.tieBreak: Higher province-wide share wins. If still tied, the teacher flips a coin on the board.

senate.appointedBy: Governor General on the Prime Minister's recommendation

parliament.governorGeneral: The teacher. Invites the party most likely to win a confidence vote to form government, reads the Throne Speech, gives Royal Assent.
parliament.confidence: A minority government must win a vote on its Throne Speech. If it loses, the Governor General asks the next party. A government that loses a budget vote falls.

federalBudget.about: Same structure as a province budget: a tax rate and the same four spending lines, plus the bridge and equalization. Costs in $B per year. Revenue is the tax rate times national GDP at the end of Year 6.

partnership.name: Private partner builds, users pay tolls

equalization.rule: Paid to provinces whose revenue at a 30% tax rate is below the cost of Standard spending. Split by the size of the gap.

federalBudget.about_levels: Same 1 to 5 levels as a province. Level 3 is Standard. At Standard with the steady bridge, the budget is close to balanced when national GDP is about $400B.
federalBudget.year7: After Royal Assent the board runs one fast fiscal year. Each province keeps its Year 6 budget. Transfers arrive as Money. Federal effects apply. Board shows each province's approval change and why.

bills.title: Borealis Founding Budget Act
bills.text: Sets the federal tax rate, the four national spending lines, the bridge plan and equalization for the first federal year.
bills.amendments: Each opposition party may propose one amendment (change one lever by one level). The House votes on each.

bills.title: Great Narrows Bridge Act
bills.text: Chooses how to rebuild the bridge: borrow and build fast, pay over 4 years, or a private partner with tolls. Use it as a 10-minute warm-up bill before C-1, or fold it into C-1 as the bridge lever.

bills.title: Open Trade Act
bills.text: Removes the paperwork fee on trade between provinces. Links to the whiteboard's free trade step. Grade 9 content: used, not assessed.

scoring.provinceScore: Approval rating. Shown live. Never a single ranked winner.

reasoningPoints.when: Every year, the Citizens' Advocate reads a 1 or 2 sentence Budget Speech. The teacher awards 0 to 3.

rubric.text: Says what you chose and why, using one number from your dashboard.
Says what you chose, why with a number, and who pays or loses (the trade-off).

reasoningPoints.effect: Each point adds 0.5 approval to every citizen group that year (constants.reasoningApprovalPerPoint). In the story, a clear explanation earns public trust.

awards.name: Most Trusted
awards.rule: Highest approval at the end of Year 6.

awards.name: Comeback
awards.rule: Biggest approval gain from the lowest point in Phase 1 to the end of Year 6.

awards.name: Fair Dealer
awards.rule: Most trades completed inside the fair price band.

awards.name: Steady Hands
awards.rule: Smallest rise in debt compared with GDP, with approval above 45.

classGoal.name: Strong Borealis
classGoal.rule: If the national average approval is 55 or more at the end of Year 6, the new federal government starts with $10B in the bank (Phase 2).

scoring.phase2: No winning party. Seats decide who governs, not who wins the unit. Reasoning points from Question Period and debate count the same as in Phase 1.
